questions.q: A product page is read 50,000 times per second and updated a few times a day. Stale data for 60 s is fine. Best first move?
options: Cache-aside with a 60 s TTL in Redis
questions.why: Read-heavy and staleness-tolerant: cache-aside with a TTL bounded by the allowed staleness. Sharding solves write or size limits, not this.

questions.q: A hot cache key expires and 10,000 requests hit the DB at once. What is this and the fix?
options: Cache stampede; request coalescing or early refresh
questions.why: Simultaneous misses on one expiring key = stampede. Coalesce (single-flight), lock per key, refresh early, or serve stale while revalidating.

questions.q: Which rate limiter allows short bursts while enforcing an average rate?
questions.why: Token bucket accumulates up to capacity B, so bursts up to B pass while the refill rate R caps the average.

questions.q: You add a 5th node to a 4-node cluster that uses hash(key) mod N. Roughly what fraction of keys move?
questions.why: With mod N almost every key changes home (only those where k mod 4 == k mod 5 stay). Consistent hashing would move ~1/5.

questions.q: Two users try to book the last seat at the same moment. Conflicts are frequent on hot events. Best approach?
options: SELECT … FOR UPDATE or an atomic conditional UPDATE
questions.why: High contention favours pessimistic locking or a single atomic `UPDATE … WHERE status='FREE'`; optimistic locking would retry constantly.

questions.q: Why add a fencing token to a Redis-based distributed lock?
options: To survive a holder whose lock expired during a GC pause
questions.why: If the lock expires while the old holder still acts, storage rejects its writes because their token is lower than the new holder's.

questions.q: Kafka topic with 6 partitions; consumer group has 8 consumers. How many consumers are active?
questions.why: Each partition goes to exactly one consumer per group, so at most 6 are busy; 2 sit idle.

questions.q: The practical way to get 'exactly once' processing with an external side effect is…
questions.why: Kafka's EOS covers Kafka-to-Kafka. For DB writes or emails, dedupe by event ID in the consumer.

questions.q: Service saves an order to Postgres and must publish OrderCreated to Kafka without losing either. Pattern?
questions.why: Write the event to an outbox table in the same DB transaction; a relay publishes it at least once.

questions.q: With N = 3 replicas, which quorum setting guarantees reads see the latest write?
questions.why: W + R > N ensures the read set overlaps the write set: 2 + 2 > 3.

questions.q: Server pushes LLM tokens to the browser one way. Simplest fitting transport?
questions.why: One-way server-to-client streaming over plain HTTP with auto-reconnect: SSE.

questions.q: Find drivers within 2 km of a rider at Uber scale. Which index idea?
options: Geohash / H3 cells and neighbour lookup
questions.why: Cell-based indexes turn 2D proximity into key lookups on the rider's cell plus neighbours, then filter by distance.
